title: clippy::too_many_arguments fires on #[near] method wrappers
summary: A public #[near] method with more than 7 parameters (counting self) makes clippy warn `too many arguments` on code the macro generates (an error under `-D warnings`). An allow on the method or at crate level silences it; an allow on the impl does not.
message: `{name}` has {count} parameters (clippy limit {max}); `cargo clippy -D warnings` will fail on the generated wrapper.

symptoms.pattern: this function has too many arguments \((?<count>\d+)/(?<max>\d+)\)

steps: Add `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on the method itself, or `#![allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` at the top of the crate root (after any `//!` docs). An attribute on the impl does not silence the generated wrapper.
Or group the arguments into a struct if you can change the JSON interface.
fix.agent: Add `#![allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` at the top of {crateRoot} (after any `//!` docs) with a short comment explaining that the #[near] wrapper repeats the arguments, then run `cargo near check --clippy`. (A `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` directly on `{name}` also works.)

autofix.comment: near-doctor F-004: the #[near] macro wrapper repeats the arguments; an allow on the impl does not silence clippy.
autofix.description: Add a crate-level #![allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] to the crate root

evidence.observed: Reproduced 2026-11-13 (macOS 15 arm64, rustc 1.100.0, cargo-near 0.23.0, near-sdk 5.30.1): `cargo near check --clippy` warned 'too many arguments (8/7)' on a #[near] method. Still warned with an allow above the #[near] impl and with an allow below #[near] above the impl. No warning with an allow on the method, nor with a crate-level allow. Corrected 2026-11-13 after scanning public repos: the first version of this rule flagged methods that already carry a method-level allow.
